_comment: WHAT EXISTS IN THIS REPO THAT A VISITOR NEVER SEES. Swept at batch 49 after finding that documented gaps had been written, recorded and reported for forty-eight batches and had never once reached a reader. That is a class of its own: nothing false, nothing stale, no schema that could not carry the truth — work completed and then not delivered. It leaves no trace, because every internal check passes.
method: Every file in data/ against the six the client actually loads; every creator and mapping field against every reference in js/; then the rendered DOM checked directly for each field that claimed to ship.

found.what: thin-gaps.json — the reason an empty category is empty
found.cost: An empty category rendered "No creators are listed for this skill yet" and nothing else, while the reason sat where the coverage report could see it.
found.fixed: visitorNote added and shipped via subject-notes.json; build warns when a gap has neither that nor a high-stakes note.

found.what: creator.jurisdictionNote — eleven sentences on what transfers across borders
found.cost: The most useful sentence on the page for any reader outside the creator's country. James Shack: "UK pensions, tax wrappers and state provision throughout. The modelling method transfers; none of the numbers do." It was authored in the same shape as languageNote, caveats and scopeNote — all three of which render from adjacent lines in creator.js — and the render for this one was simply never written.
found.fixed: Renders on the creator page and the card as "Where this applies".

found.what: status: dormant on the creator CARD
found.reached: NO — the detail page had it, the card did not
found.cost: On a category page, which is where a visitor actually chooses, a channel silent for over a year looked identical to one that posted this morning. Half-shipped is its own failure: the schema change, the audit, the home-page counts and the detail page all landed, and the one surface between them did not.
found.fixed: Card meta now shows both non-active states.

found.cost: Smaller, same shape. The vendor/institution distinction matters most in a list where a reader is comparing.
found.fixed: Card now shows Company channel / Organisation.

found.what: Critic scarcity — 21 critics across 240 creators, 30 of 183 populated skills
found.cost: A page with no dissenting voice simply omits the section, so the two cases are indistinguishable: no critic exists, and we never looked. The project reports this internally with its denominator every run and told a reader nothing.
found.fixed: Colophon section 05, with the numbers computed at render. DELIBERATELY NOT per-page: rule 11 settled that a notice appearing on four pages in five trains a reader to skim the warnings that matter.

correctlyInternal._note: Not everything unshipped is a failure. These are records of how the work was done, and a reader is owed the conclusion rather than the method.
correctlyInternal.probed.json: 267 handles with rejection reasons — a research ledger.
correctlyInternal.handle-rescues.json: Which creators the fallback search had to rescue.
correctlyInternal.field-audit.json / procedure-audit.json: Audits of our own process and schema.
correctlyInternal.critic-gaps.json: Empty by design until the end of Phase 2.
correctlyInternal.domain-notes.retired / .corrected / .ope: The arc of measurements written, confirmed and falsified.
correctlyInternal.thin-gaps rule18 blocks: Which sub-areas were probed. The conclusion ships as visitorNote; the method is ours.
correctlyInternal.creator.catalogue: The measurement the prose is interpolated from — it reaches the page as the sentence, which is the point.
correctlyInternal.creator.addedLater / language: Provenance and a field that is 'en' for every record.

openProposals.what: findings-ledger.json — 14 claims tested about our own work, 10 falsified, 4 of them live on the site before being caught
openProposals.case: The most on-brand thing this site could publish and the strongest evidence its method is real. A section saying plainly that we test our own claims, that most did not survive, and that four were wrong in public before we caught them.
openProposals.against: It is a page about us on a site meant to be about skills, and the numbers are unflattering in a way a reader has no way to calibrate.

openProposals.case: Section 04 explains that depth was allocated by measured appetite but shows no number, so a reader cannot check the reasoning against any particular skill.
openProposals.against: A view count on a skill page invites it to be read as a recommendation.

openProposals.what: reputation-drift.json — 11 creators whose current catalogue no longer matches their reputation
openProposals.case: Genuinely useful to a reader who arrives expecting the old channel.
openProposals.against: It is a public judgement about named people who are not listed here and cannot answer it.
openProposals.status: DEFERRED BY THE OWNER at batch 33 — 'make sure the data exists in a usable shape, decide at the end of Phase 2'. Still pending.
